messages.content: I just finished 'Thinking, Fast and Slow'. Can you help me turn my highlights into a short set of reading notes?
Sure. A good structure is: the core idea (System 1 vs System 2), three or four key biases with an example each, and what you want to apply.
My main takeaways were anchoring, the planning fallacy and loss aversion. I want to remember the planning fallacy most.
For the planning fallacy, note the remedy Kahneman suggests: reference-class forecasting, i.e. look at how long similar projects actually took.
Good. Next I want to read 'The Righteous Mind'. I'll keep notes in the same format.
